notes:
Gate passed on the fake backend (G1 to G9, no warnings) for gh.clarklabucb/newerapumps_python3 at commit b8e3d0214ded43734ad22fa378b5bd408010f109. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: this is a direct Driver, not the card's SerialDriver, because new_era3.py assembles every command from a pump address and a token (<n>DIRINF, <n>RAT<value>UH, <n>DIA<mm>, <n>STP, <n>RAT0UH) and never writes a literal command line; a command table cannot reproduce those bytes and gate G7 cannot find their first token in the clone. The native symbol is the card's class pump_control3:PumpControl; the driver uses only the pyserial handle that class stores as self.ser (pump_control3.py:23), and native.py opens that handle without importing the GUI or PyQt5. The fake is a protocol stand-in for the handle, not a recording: its start rate, start diameter and start address are test data marked '# placeholder' in fake.py, never facts or limits. NOT COVERED: the clone exposes no volume measurement, so this driver reads and writes only the signed flow-rate set point and the syringe diameter and its actions are start and stop; it reports no dispensed volume. flow_rate and diameter are Limit.operator_required because no text file states a device range; site-limits.example.json supplies example ranges only (0 to 10000 uL/h, 0.1 to 50 mm), and the four BD syringe sizes in the GUI are not treated as a device bound. The package is R2 because the pump moves liquid; the native stop is the broadcast *STP of new_era3.stop_all, and x-cap.clarklabucb.stop_pump.v1 is the safe-state action (<n>STP then <n>RAT0UH). No hardware backend was run, no instrument was tried, and reviewed_by stays null. check-report.json was generated by the final gate run; its digest is the one above.
